I farm the same 5 mu the way I usually do here in Quzhou, wheat first and then maize after wheat. I did not start from zero. I start from what worked before and change only a little. I went to primary school, so I do look at what the seed dealer says, but in the end I still trust what I saw in nearby fields. If a neighbor used a better wheat seed and got a fuller ear, I will use that kind too. Same for maize, I will use hybrid seed because around here it gives steadier yield.

For fertilizer, I will not hold back too much. Fertilizer costs money, that is true, but losing yield costs more. On my 5 mu, I can still manage carefully. For wheat, I will put the base fertilizer down first, then chase some nitrogen at jointing. Since I have well water, I will water wheat about 3 times if the year is normal: one before winter if the soil is dry, one at jointing, and one at grain filling if needed. For maize, I will sow right after wheat harvest so I do not lose moisture, then I will topdress nitrogen when it is knee-high or a bit taller. I will water maize about 2 times in a normal year, mainly around big flare stage and grain filling if the ground is dry. I will spray when I see a real problem, but in a normal year I count about 2 sprays for each crop. I will keep rotary tillage because on 5 mu it is practical and not too expensive, and it fits the wheat-maize rotation I already know.
